claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are uniformly solid.
The starting nanoparticles have a nominal equiatomic composition of approximately 20 at.% each Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu.
Local compositional inhomogeneities govern the onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu-enriched regions are preferential sites for defect formation.
Cu-enriched or defect-rich regions have lower local melting temperatures than the surrounding nanoparticle.
Compositional fluctuations reduce the local melting temperature through increased chemical disorder and defect concentration.
Defect-rich grain boundaries act as structural mediators that lower the local melting threshold.
Cu-rich or defect-dense zones initiate localized liquid-phase nucleation.
With continued heating, locally melted regions grow and coalesce through enhanced atomic diffusion.
Melting will begin at discrete Cu-enriched regions rather than uniformly throughout the nanoparticle.
A melting front will propagate from the initial Cu-enriched nucleation sites across the nanoparticle.
An oxygen-free inert environment avoids oxidation during heating.
Rapid thermal processing can preserve local compositional nonuniformity because it does not provide complete homogenization.
The proposed inhomogeneity-controlled melting mechanism should be most significant for rapidly processed nanoparticles.
Prolonged annealing can produce sufficient compositional homogenization to alter the melting behavior.
The proposed behavior may differ between nanoparticles and bulk FeNiCrCoCu materials.
Rapid cooling will yield a batch with natural compositional inhomogeneities, whereas slow cooling will homogenize the nanoparticles.
The exact Cu-enrichment threshold required to initiate localized melting is not yet quantified.
Identical melting behavior in homogenized and non-homogenized batches, without spatial correlation between Cu enrichment and liquid nucleation, would falsify the hypothesis.
